newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: New pre-trial date for Singapore corruption case.
newsitem.headline: New pre-trial date for Singapore corruption case.

text.p: A pre-trial hearing for a Singapore official facing charges of corruption involving at least HK$12 million (US$1.55 million) has been adjourned for three weeks, the official's lawyer said on Saturday.

Jason Lim told Reuters that his client, Taw Cheng Kong, would appear on March 14 for a pre-trial hearing into eight charges arising from investments made through Hong Kong asset management firm Rockefeller & Co (Far East) Ltd.
Lim declined to provide any further details.

Taw, a regional manager at the Government of Singapore Investment Corp (GIC), was charged on November 5 with receiving bribes from Kevin Lee Kwok-wing, then managing director of Rockefeller & Co, to buy specific shares. There have been no reports of Lee being charged.
Taw has since been suspended from the GIC, which is responsible for managing part of Singapore's huge foreign reserves that hit Singapore $107.75 billion (US$75.88 billion) in December.
The GIC also holds stocks, bonds and property in 25 nations.
Singapore's government prides itself as being one of the cleanest in the world and corruption cases involving state officials are rare.
Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament in December that GIC had incurred some losses in its investments through Rockefeller & Co but he declined to disclose the extent.
